title: Giants release veteran wide receiver Darius Slayton
content:
The New York Giants announced Monday that they have released veteran wide receiver Darius Slayton. Slayton, a fifth-round pick in 2019, was the longest-tenured Giant, sticking around through multiple head coaching changes. Slayton was preparing to play his eighth season with the franchise.

“Grateful for my time in NY,” Slayton posted on social media shortly after his release was announced. “7 years a Giant nothing but love for one of the most prestigious organizations in the NFL. Excited to see what’s next.”

The move saves the Giants $3.2 million against the 2026 salary cap. Slayton had signed a three-year, $36 million deal with the Giants ahead of the 2025 season. Now, he’s a free agent. He’s not eligible for waivers as a vested veteran and can sign elsewhere.

Slayton fluctuated up and down the Giants’ wide receiver depth chart during his time in New York. But no matter where he was entering the season, the deep threat almost always figured out a way to emerge as a key contributor. Slayton, who tallied 296 receptions for 4,435 yards and 22 touchdowns in New York, led the Giants in receiving four times in his first five seasons. His best season came as a rookie, when he hauled in 48 passes for 740 yards and eight touchdowns.

The release of Slayton is only somewhat of a surprise, however, as the veteran was reportedly on the roster bubble and was part of trade speculation as the Giants were cutting down their roster a little more than a week ago. Slayton made the initial 53-man group, only to be cut on Monday.

“Nothing really,” Slayton said last week when asked what it’s like to see his name as a potential trade target. “It’s not the first time, probably won’t be the last time. But I really don’t pay it too much of mind, honestly. I just take it day by day.

“You kind of just figure out the league the more you’re around. At the end of the day, you control what you can control and let the rest fall where it may.”

The veteran receiver underwent a double sports hernia surgery this spring but said last week that he was feeling “pretty good” as training camp wrapped up.

“I wouldn’t say 100 yet, but definitely turning in the right direction,” Slayton said.

Cutting Slayton leaves the Giants’ depth chart somewhat thin, with only four receivers on the 53-man roster: Malik Nabers, rookie Malachi Fields, Darnell Mooney and Odell Beckham Jr. Braxton Berrios, Dalen Cambre, Jalin Hyatt and Charlie Jones are on the practice squad, and Berrios will be part of the Giants’ game-day roster, either after being added to the 53-man roster or as a practice squad elevation.

Nabers’ Week 1 availability as he returns from a torn ACL is unknown. The Giants open the 2026 season Sunday night at home against the NFC East rival Dallas Cowboys.
